title: Shared Test State Leaks Beyond Its Scope
pattern: A test mutates shared globals, environment variables, files, database state, or static singletons without complete isolation or guaranteed restoration of the original state.
why_bad: It violates test isolation (hermeticity) and leaks state modifications across tests [507, 657]. Tests become non-deterministic, flaky, and highly order-dependent, unsafe to run concurrently, and produce confusing failures located far from the actual bug [331, 460, 507, 658].
detection: Shared state (mutable static globals, environment variables, shared files, shared databases, singletons) is changed inside a test without teardown/rollback or a scoped guard that restores the prior state on every exit path, so other tests can observe the mutation.
counterexample: Per-test database instances and file namespaces; suitably isolated thread-local state; scoped RAII guards that automatically restore the value on drop, when no concurrent test can observe the temporary shared state.
fix: Prefer per-test resources so each test is hermetic [507]. If shared state is unavoidable, restore its original value with guaranteed teardown (a `tearDown` block, an automated wrapper, or a static setup/teardown setter such as `setTestingInstance`) and prevent concurrent observers via serialization or process isolation where needed [310, 376, 620, 657, 658].
source:
